events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 1015 AM EDT/915 AM CDT/.

* At 850 AM EDT/750 AM CDT/, a severe thunderstorm capable of
producing waterspouts was located over O Tower, moving east at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
S Tower, V Tower, O Tower, C Tower, St George Island, and K Tower.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Wabash River from Montezuma through Mount Carmel.

White River from Edwardsport through Hazleton.

.Minor flooding continues along the White River from Edwardsport
downriver with the crest already past Hazleton.  Minor flooding also
continues on the Wabash River from Montezuma down to Mount Carmel
with the crest approaching Vincennes. Rain amounts with scattered
storms Wednesday evening are not expected to impact main stem river
levels.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Montezuma.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Montezuma agricultural levee is overtopped.
Fourteen hundred acres of low bottomlands flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 16.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 AM EDT Tuesday was 18.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 7.5 feet Friday,
September 04.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
